name: Budgeting MEP Upgrades for ADU and Multi-Unit Conversions in Los Angeles

mainEntity.name: What should I budget for required electrical, plumbing, and HVAC upgrades when converting an older Los Angeles house and garage into multi-unit living with an ADU?
mainEntity.text: What should I budget for required electrical, plumbing, and HVAC upgrades when converting an older Los Angeles house and garage into multi-unit living with an ADU?

acceptedAnswer.text: Transforming an older Los Angeles home and garage into multi-unit living with an ADU affects every major system. Many budgets underestimate the cost of bringing **electrical, plumbing, and HVAC** up to current standards. Electrically, older 60–100 amp services are often insufficient once you add a full kitchen, laundry, and HVAC for an ADU. Plan for a **panel upgrade**, new subpanels, dedicated kitchen and HVAC circuits, and GFCI/AFCI protection as required by current codes. If you anticipate EV charging or all-electric appliances, future-proofing with higher capacity is wise. On the plumbing side, adding a new bathroom and kitchen can strain old supply lines and sewer capacity. You may need upsized water service, replacement of aged galvanized lines, and new sewer laterals or tie-ins. Long runs from the main house to a detached garage ADU require trenching and careful slope planning. For HVAC, each dwelling usually needs independent systems. Options include extending existing ducted systems (if appropriately sized), installing new gas or electric furnaces, or using **ductless mini-splits** for zoning flexibility. Energy codes may require certain efficiency levels and controls. Building an accurate budget means asking contractors for **itemized system upgrades**, not just square-foot pricing, and allowing contingency for hidden defects revealed during demolition.
acceptedAnswer.description: Plan for service upgrades to the main electrical panel, new subpanels, additional plumbing supply and sewer capacity, and independent heating and cooling systems. Older homes often require rewiring, new circuits, and modern ducted or ductless systems to safely and comfortably support both the main house and ADU.
